LILACS: 1/1 seed tested (Rocha 2017, via L2); effect items verified only via a narrowed sub-query because of BVS 502/timeouts. Research index: generic framing 0/4 seeds in top 100 (2 seeds not indexed) and 5/7 V items in top 100.

volume_estimate_after_dedup: Raw counts: OpenAlex OA-1 ∪ OA-2 = 625 (464 + 266 − 105). OA-3 = 146 and OA-4 = 311, so the OpenAlex upper bound is 1,082 before cross-branch overlap. SciELO: 175 + 135 + 67 = 377 records, including the same article listed in several collections (roughly 1.5–2x duplication in the samples seen). LILACS: 416 + 107 = 523. Raw total about 1,980. SciELO and LILACS records largely duplicate OpenAlex PT/ES records and each other. My estimate is about 1,100–1,400 unique records after deduplication: roughly 750–900 for the effect arms plus 350–450 context records, which should be flagged 'context'. Trade-off: dropping the generic outcome terms 'perinatal', 'newborns' and 'gestational age' and the OA-2 language branch would cut volume but lose Dutra 2019, so the broad version is recommended. The volume is screenable in about 10–15 reviewer-hours at title/abstract stage.
issues_and_limits: Rate limits: Firecrawl (about 13 requests/min, shared) and Parallel (repeated 429s) stopped several calls. Every failed call is logged and the affected queries were retried; one OpenAlex check (X AND E2 AND O2, language:pt|es) returned an empty Firecrawl answer and was not counted.

BVS/LILACS portal (pesquisa.bvsalud.org) gave 502 Bad Gateway on several attempts and timeouts on others, and worked intermittently. The DeCS (mh:) version of L1 is untested, and a strict L1 AND known-item test could not be completed (recall shown via a narrowed sub-query).
SciELO counts are at record level and include duplicates across collections (scl, spa, col, etc.). The default 'Todos os índices' does not include author names.

SciELO tokenization defect: a word next to punctuation in the title or abstract (e.g. 'Apodi,') is not matched as a bare token or phrase, but is matched with truncation (Apodi*). Phrase queries in SciELO are therefore unreliable; prefer truncation. This likely explains the brief's note that a naive phrase query returned 0.

OpenAlex: no wildcards (HTTP 400), no accent folding, and incomplete stemming of accented PT words, so all inflections must be spelled out. Camacho & Mejía has no abstract in OpenAlex, and title-only matching is fragile for similar econ papers.

Seeds Dias (ReStud) and Calzada (JAERE) are not in the PubMed-centric research index, SciELO or LILACS. Economics papers depend on OpenAlex and web search, so add a separate EconLit/RePEc/NBER/SSRN step in the main SQ1.

The extended validation sets V and X were found during this calibration (via web and research-index searches), not fixed in advance. Recall measured on them is optimistic and should be reported as development-set recall, not independent validation.
The SciELO S1 recommended addition (fumigat*) and the OpenAlex outcome additions were not re-tested in SciELO/LILACS (counts for S1 and L1 are for the strings as tested).

Dossiê ABRASCO (2015) has no DOI. Identify it by ISBN 9788598768809 (EPSJV) / 9788577432561 (Expressão Popular) and the ARCA/Fiocruz handle (arca.fiocruz.br/items/95e08e29-61d4-461e-a5d6-dd880d2592fb); OpenAlex has it as W2345103675 without DOI. A 2018 article on its Spanish version has DOI 10.18472/sustdeb.v9n1.2018.29594.

Silva et al. 2011 (São Francisco Valley congenital defects, PMID 21625789) and the Rev Bras Promoç Saúde 2017 study of fetal mortality in Ceará's 10th health region: DOIs not verified. Rigotto et al. 2013 DOI (10.1590/S1415-790X2013000300019) was confirmed through SciELO, but the OpenAlex title-search record lacks it; recall was tested by DOI.
syntax_findings: OpenAlex title_and_abstract.search: uppercase AND/OR/NOT and parentheses work (A OR B = 12,860 vs 7,856 + 5,040; NOT reduces 7,856 to 7,820). Quoted strings become stemmed phrases. Several title_and_abstract.search filters separated by commas are ANDed. language:pt|es and doi:a|b|c filters combine with search filters.

OpenAlex: wildcard 'agrot*' returns HTTP 400. Accents are not folded (agrotóxicos 7,856 vs agrotoxicos 1,318). agrotóxico (1,069) is not stemmed to agrotóxicos, while plaguicida = plaguicidas (5,040) and pesticide = pesticides (316,429). 'birthweight' is a separate token from "birth weight".

SciELO search.scielo.org: AND/OR, parentheses, quotes and * truncation work; it is accent-insensitive (agrotóxicos = agrotoxicos = 895). The field indices doi:, pid:, ti:, ab:, au:, in:, la: work (used doi:/pid: for recall testing). Some records (e.g. Cremonese 2012) lack a DOI in the index, so test them by pid. Bare tokens next to punctuation can be unindexed, so use truncation (Apodi*, Jaguaribe*).

BVS portal: free-text with * truncation and AND/OR works, and filter[db][]=LILACS restricts to LILACS (facet confirms). Longer queries with mh: descriptors coincided with 502 errors. Short truncated stems produced unrelated cardiology records.

incidental_relevant_studies.title: Impacts of pesticide exposure on birth outcomes and child health in Brazil (Januzzi, Cardoso, Rodrigues; UFV/ENABER)

incidental_relevant_studies.title: Armed conflict and birthweight: The role of organized violence and anti-coca fumigation in Colombia
incidental_relevant_studies.why: Aerial fumigation and birthweight in Colombia; close analogue to the aerial-method treatment.

incidental_relevant_studies.title: Pesticide exposure, birth size, and gestational age in the ISA birth cohort, Costa Rica
incidental_relevant_studies.why: Banana-plantation cohort with aerially applied mancozeb (fungicide). The closest chemical and crop analogue to Ceará's banana dose.

incidental_relevant_studies.title: Aerial application of mancozeb and urinary ethylene thiourea (ETU) concentrations among pregnant women in Costa Rica: the ISA study
incidental_relevant_studies.why: Exposure-pathway evidence that aerial banana fungicide spraying reaches pregnant women. Supports the first stage of the mechanism.
